title: Product PRD: Unified Inference — Overview, Roadmap, Pricing & Packaging (v2026-11)
author: Maya Thompson
summary: This document consolidates the product overview, prioritized requirements, high-level design notes, roadmap milestones, and pricing & packaging recommendations for the Unified Inference product line. It is intended for product, engineering, sales, and customer success teams planning Q4 2026 launches and early 2027 feature rollouts.
background_and_problem: Background: Redwood's Unified Inference initiative aims to deliver a single API and operational surface that provides consistent latency, cost controls, and deployment flexibility across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private modes. Problem: Customers and internal stakeholders are asking for clearer packaging and an aligned roadmap so engineering prioritization, go-to-market positioning, and sales proposals deliver predictable economics and upgrade paths. Without a consolidated PRD we risk inconsistent messaging, misaligned milestones, and missed revenue uplift from packaging changes.
objectives_and_scope:
Primary objectives:
- Provide a single, coherent product definition for Unified Inference (core API, routing, caching, and runtime options).
- Define a prioritized set of functional and non-functional requirements for the next two quarters.
- Publish a roadmap with milestones and release criteria.
- Define pricing tiers, add-ons, and recommended upgrade paths for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private customers.
Scope in this PRD:
- Included: API surface (generation, chat, embeddings), routing & fallback policies, caching/batching features, quantization/optimization recommendations, pricing & packaging for GA.
- Excluded: Lower-level kernel optimizations, per-customer on-prem installation scripts (documented separately in eng-private-deployments).
functional_requirements: REQ-001: Unified REST/SDK endpoints for text generation, chat, and embeddings with consistent parameter semantics across deployment modes.
REQ-002: Model catalog API exposing verified performance profiles and compatible fallback variants (e.g., fp16, 8-bit, quantized variants).
REQ-003: Smart routing policy: config-driven routing by latency SLO, cost target, region, and customer tier with fallbacks.
REQ-004: Prefix/KV caching API and auto-eviction policy with metrics surfaced in Console per route/model.
REQ-005: Autoscaling and reserved-capacity binding for Dedicated with burst-to-hosted policy during cold starts.
REQ-006: Streaming responses and function/tool calling support with trace headers for observability.
REQ-007: Per-route rollout controls (canary, A/B, automatic rollback on quality regressions).
REQ-008: Billing metadata emitted per-request: model_variant, quantization_profile, batch_id, and request_cost_estimate.
REQ-009: Customer-managed keys integration for Private deployments (KMS/HSM) and audit-log export for compliance.
nonfunctional_requirements: NFR-001: Latency P50 target of <= 60ms for small chat messages (<= 64 tokens) on Hosted for selected low-latency variants.
NFR-002: 99.9% availability for Hosted API endpoints (per release SLA objective).
NFR-003: Cost-per-token reduction targets: 25% lower median cost via batching/caching recommendations for common workloads versus baseline.
NFR-004: End-to-end tracing available and integrated with Console; error budgets tracked per model-route.
NFR-005: Support for sequence lengths up to 8k tokens with graceful degradation profiles defined for >8k.
design_spec_overview:
High-level design:
- Serving runtime exposes a trait-based model adapter so different model architectures plug into the same API surface.
- Request flow: ingress -> auth -> routing policy -> runtime execution -> caching layer -> billing emitter -> response stream.
- Routing: policy engine evaluates (latency_slo, cost_budget, region, capacity) and routes to a compatible model_variant.
- Caching: two layers — prefix cache (request-level) and KV-cache (context window). Cache hit/miss metrics are emitted to Console.
- Observability: tracing hooks at each stage, token-level cost attribution, per-route dashboards for latency, throughput, and quality regressions.
- Security: customer-managed KMS hooks for Private; role-based access for Console controls.
Design notes and tradeoffs:
- We prioritize a consistent API over exposing every runtime optimization detail; advanced power users can opt-in to explicit variant flags.
- Batching heuristics are workload-driven and will be tunable via per-customer profiles; default heuristics target median latency SLOs.
roadmap_and_milestones:
Roadmap (high level):
- Q4 2026 (Nov 2026): GA of Unified Inference Core (API parity across modes, basic routing, prefix caching, Console dashboards). Release criteria: all REQs 001-005 implemented, end-to-end tests, and SLO verification.
- Q1 2027 (Jan–Mar): Advanced routing (cost-aware multi-variant routing), quantified batching profiles, and Dedicated autoscaling primitives.
- Q2 2027: Private deployment improvements (air-gapped packaging), KMS/HSM deep integrations, and enterprise compliance add-ons.
- Q3 2027: Redwood Optimize integration: automated quantization/selection recommendations and quality-aware rollouts.
Milestones and owners:
- Nov 2026 GA release: Product (Maya Thompson), Eng (Lead: Alex Kim), SRE (Lead: Priya Natarajan).
- Jan 2027 routing v2: Product (Diego Alvarez), Eng (Lead: Samir Patel).
pricing_and_packaging:
Pricing principles:
- Predictable economics (clear per-token and capacity pricing) with upgrade paths that reward committed Dedicated capacity.
- Add-on pricing for advanced observability, extended retention, and compliance packages.
- Clear differentiation between Hosted (usage-first), Dedicated (reserved capacity), and Private (platform + support).
Recommended tiers (examples):
1) Hosted - Developer: $0.0008 per prompt-token / $0.0012 per generated-token; 30-day usage quota & self-serve dashboard.
2) Hosted - Team: $0.0006 per prompt-token / $0.0009 per generated-token; rate limits 5x Developer; includes basic batching suggestions and 30-day logs.
3) Dedicated - Standard Commit: $12,000/month per reserved GPU pool (example) + $0.0004 per generated-token beyond pooled throughput; SLA 99.9%.
4) Private - Enterprise: Platform license (negotiated) + deployment fee + optional support tiers (Gold/Platinum). Includes KMS/HSM integration and compliance add-ons.
Packaging notes:
- Offer a ‘Migration Pack’ for Dedicated customers: 3 months of discounted overprovisioning to smooth cutover.
- Add-ons: Extended audit log retention (90/365 days), Model Verification service (per-model onboarding), Redwood Optimize subscription for automated cost/quality recommendations.
Pricing tests and rollout:
- Pilot discounts for top 10 existing Dedicated customers in Q4 2026.
- A/B test price elasticity on Team tier in Q1 2027 with targeted onboarding playbooks.
release_notes:
Release v2026-11 (GA):
- Feature highlights: Unified REST/SDK parity across Hosted/Dedicated/Private, prefix caching, model catalog with verified profiles, basic smart routing, and Console dashboards for per-route latency and cost.
- Known limitations: Advanced quantization recommendations and Redwood Optimize integrations are limited to experimental flag in GA. Private air-gapped packaging is beta.
- Migration guidance: Use migration-playbook (see related_pages) for Dedicated customers; enable prefix-caching in staging and run the provided eval prompt sets to validate regressions.
- Rollout: Gradual rollout by customer tier starting Nov 30, 2026 with automated rollback triggers for quality regressions (per-route thresholds).
rollout_and_migration_plan:
Rollout steps (numbered):
1) Internal soft-launch: release to internal teams and selected partners, monitor SLOs and Console metrics for 2 weeks.
2) Pilot customers: onboard 8–12 pilot customers segmented by workload profile (chat-heavy, embeddings-heavy, batch inference).
3) Tiered public rollout: open Team tier sign-ups, then expand Developer and Dedicated exposure.
4) Communication: update docs site, publish migration-playbook and SDK samples, host two customer webinars.
5) Post-launch: weekly Q/A and postmortem cadence for first 8 weeks; iterate on pricing/packaging based on usage telemetry.
success_metrics_and_kpis: Launch stability: < 0.5 production incidents impacting >= 5 customers in first 30 days.
Adoption: 25% growth in new Hosted API sign-ups for Unified Inference routes in Q1 2027.
Cost effectiveness: average per-token cost improvement >= 20% for customers adopting batching/caching recommendations.
Commercial: convert 15% of Team tier customers to Dedicated within 6 months via Migration Pack.

open_risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Quality regressions when routing to quantized/compatible variants. Mitigation: require automated evals and canary rollouts with rollback on metric regressions.
Risk: Pricing complexity causing friction in trials. Mitigation: clear examples and a free credits migration pack for early adopters.
Risk: Dedicated autoscaling edge-cases under tail loads. Mitigation: sizing guidance, burst-to-hosted policies, and runbook updates in eng-sre.
